name: Wen Junsheng
current_role: One of the 10 actual controllers (Wen family concert group) of Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ)
profile: Wen Junsheng (温均生) is a member of the founding Wen family behind Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig/poultry producer founded by his father Wen Beifen in 1983. He remains on the 10-person actual-controller group named under the family's renewed concert-party agreement (2025), per the company's 2026 interim report.
interesting_fact: Per Jiemian, he is Wen Beifen's eldest son and the father of Wen Jiaolong, the first third-generation family member added as an actual controller and to the Wens board.
notes: No personal profile/executive post found; low public profile. Approach via Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn, tel published 0766-2292926). Alive status not explicitly confirmed, but listed as controller in Aug 2026 filing.

name: Xu Xizhong
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Hubei Sanxia New Building Materials (600293.SH); current post unknown
profile: Xu Xizhong (许锡忠) controlled Shanghai-listed float-glass maker Sanxia New Materials (三峡新材), together with his vehicle Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment (海南宗宣达实业), and chaired its board; the company also owned mobile-phone distributor Shenzhen Hengbo. By 2025 the company was controlled by Dangyang City Investment and chaired by Xie Pule.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he chaired Sanxia New Materials while also chairing Shenzhen Weikangde Investment Group, Jiangxi Chaosheng Mining and Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment, per the company's 2019 annual report.
deep_cut_fact: His career began as a department manager at a garment factory in Laowu township, Chaoyang county, Guangdong; he later ran a restaurant (Haomen Yeda Jiulou) in Puning as general manager before becoming chairman of Shenzhen Xinzhen Co.
notes: Hurun listing only 2017. He has since lost control of Sanxia New Materials (now state-controlled) and his shares were frozen in 2019 litigation; a Dec 2025 SSE regulatory warning named him as former chairman. Likely no longer UHNW and not a good outreach target; no published contact found.

name: Olga Polizzi
current_role: Deputy Chairman and Director of Design, Rocco Forte Hotels; owner of The Polizzi Collection (Hotel Tresanton, Hotel Endsleigh, The Star)
profile: Olga Polizzi CBE (b. 1946), daughter of Charles Forte, is a British hotelier and interior designer who co-founded Rocco Forte Hotels with her brother Sir Rocco Forte, where she is deputy chairman and design director. She also owns The Polizzi Collection: Hotel Tresanton in Cornwall (bought 1998), Hotel Endsleigh in Devon (2004) and The Star in Alfriston, Sussex.
interesting_fact: She joined the family business only after her first husband died, starting in Forte's design department where budgets were so tight 'we couldn't spend more than £8 on a metre of fabric'.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager she and Rocco worked at the airport making sandwiches, and she also worked in the Café Royal kitchens; a keen gardener, she opens her Sussex garden every year for the local hospice and hospital. She calls herself 'a complete Eeyore' next to her optimistic brother.

public_contacts.value: sophie@thepolizzicollection.com (Sophie Grounds, Director of Communications, The Polizzi Collection)

notes: Also a former Conservative Westminster councillor (Lancaster Gate). Mother of TV's 'Hotel Inspector' Alex Polizzi. Best route: Polizzi Collection comms director.

name: Zeng Hui
current_role: Co-founder and ~18.85% shareholder (one of the controlling shareholders) of Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic (603283.SH)
profile: Zeng Hui (曾慧, b. 1977) co-founded Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic in 2007 with Sun Feng; the Shanghai-listed company makes automated/intelligent manufacturing and inspection equipment for consumer-electronics makers. She served as general manager from 2015 and remains a top shareholder, directly holding 18.85% as of Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Secote's 36Kr company profile lists her as founder and general manager with a junior-college (dazhuan) education, building the company from a 2007 startup into a listed automation-equipment maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote she did sales work at Shanghai Liangrui Electronics (1999-2002) and then was deputy general manager of Yanling Automation Equipment Factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong Economic Development Zone (2002-2007).
notes: Feb 2026 SSE filing confirms her 18.85% stake (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-02-28/1224987773.PDF); an Aug 2025 company notice mentions her separately from directors/officers, so she may no longer hold an executive post. No published personal contact; route via Secote board office.

name: Huang Jiadi
current_role: Chairman and President, Royal Group Co. (皇氏集团, formerly Huangshi Dairy; 002329.SZ), Nanning, Guangxi
profile: Huang Jiadi (黄嘉棣, b. 1962) is founder-chairman and controlling shareholder of Royal Group, a Guangxi dairy company built around buffalo milk that listed in Shenzhen in 2010. In July 2026 he agreed to sell ~5.8% to a Shenzhen green/low-carbon investment partnership, keeping ~20% and control.
interesting_fact: He has positioned the company around buffalo milk; in a Feb 2026 interview he cited a dairy-buffalo germplasm 'chip' breakthrough and the birth of a calf from embryos imported from Pakistan.
deep_cut_fact: A Guangxi University graduate and senior engineer, he started as an engineer at the Guangxi Architectural Comprehensive Design Institute and was development manager at the Shenzhen Shatoujiao Free Trade Zone development company before dairy; he is a three-term president of the Guangxi Dairy Association.
notes: Company has an agrivoltaics (农光互补) buffalo-farm project in Binyang county, which may interest an energy podcast. Company and he received regulatory warning letters over disclosure (2023-2024). Also president of the Shanghai Guangxi Chamber of Commerce and CKGSB Guangxi alumni association.

name: Josette Ades
current_role: Private investor; directly holds ~6.4% (8.1M Class A shares) of Organogenesis Holdings (NASDAQ: ORGO)
profile: Josette Ades is the spouse of Alan A. Ades, co-founder of Canton, Massachusetts regenerative-medicine/wound-care company Organogenesis Holdings. A June 2025 Schedule 13D/A lists her as directly owning 8,112,497 ORGO shares (~6.4%); the founding Ades/Erani/Nussdorf holders then said they no longer act as a 'group'.
interesting_fact: She was a reporting person in the Ades/Erani/Nussdorf founder-family Schedule 13D on Organogenesis, whose shares are counted within her husband Alan Ades's ~17.6% beneficial stake.
notes: Very private: no public profile found beyond SEC filings (signed via attorney-in-fact William R. Kolb). Not an executive; outreach realistically only via the Ades family / Organogenesis. Alive status not confirmed.

name: Liu Chenyan
current_role: Director (former chairman to Apr 2025) and major shareholder, Wangsu Science & Technology (300017.SZ); controls Cloudsway via Fromindo Limited
profile: Liu Chengyan (刘成彦, b. 1964; listed as 'Liu Chenyan') joined CDN/edge-cloud provider Wangsu Science & Technology as COO in 2001, a year after its founding by Chen Baozhen, became its second-largest shareholder and long-time chairman after its 2009 listing. He stepped down as chairman on 7 Apr 2025 for personal reasons, the same day he completed buying Wangsu's 42.3% stake in AI-cloud unit Cloudsway for RMB105.7m.
interesting_fact: In 2025 he personally (via Fromindo Limited) bought Wangsu's 42.2997% stake in Cloudsway Pte. Ltd., a cloud MSP focused on AI model-as-a-service for large-model inference, for RMB105.75m.
deep_cut_fact: A Southeast University graduate, he worked at China Machine Press and the China Association for Science and Technology's management-science research centre, helped set up Beijing Yimai e-mail company, and was COO of China Wanwang (HiChina) in 1999-2000 before joining Wangsu.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/edge-cloud theme (CDN, edge computing, AI inference cloud via Cloudsway). Times Weekly reports he bought an 18% Wangsu stake in 2005 for RMB1.8m (https://m.163.com/dy/article/JV2KQS900519APGA.html). Current director status after 2025 not re-verified.

name: The Oughtred family
current_role: Family owners of William Jackson Food Group (Hessle, Hull); family on board incl. Chairwoman Sonya Eastaugh and NEDs Nicholas, Mark and Patrick Oughtred
profile: The Oughtreds are the descendant family behind William Jackson Food Group, a sixth-generation Hull food business founded in 1851. The group sold Aunt Bessie's and now owns Abel & Cole, Jacksons Bakery, Belazu (incl. Miso Tasty), Lottie Shaw's and Wellocks. Nicholas Oughtred chaired it for 16 years until 2022; family shareholder Sonya Eastaugh is chairwoman, with CEO Paul Murphy since April 2025.
interesting_fact: Founder William Jackson opened his first shop in 1851 on his wedding day; the company later pioneered horse-drawn deliveries (1908) and a travelling shop (1952), and seventh-generation shareholders are now taking an active role.
deep_cut_fact: Sixth-generation family director Mark Oughtred, a non-executive on the group board with a background in fresh-produce and horticulture marketing, also serves as a Special Constable.
notes: A family, not one person: pick a spokesperson (Chairwoman Sonya Eastaugh or Nicholas Oughtred). HQ: The Riverside Building, Livingstone Road, Hessle HU13 0DZ (business address). Site blocks scripted access; email on site is obfuscated.
